sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and fixed admin email
sections.what: Sets up the imports, storage helpers, the Node.js runtime setting, and the fixed admin email address.
sections.why: Keeps the admin identity in one place.
sections.watch_out: Changing the email here changes which account this route treats as the admin.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Create the admin account
sections.what: Creates the admin account only when the secret is correct and no admin exists yet, and the password is long enough.
sections.why: Runs once so the admin account exists before anyone else signs up.
sections.watch_out: Error messages from failures are sent back to the caller, which can reveal internal detail.

summary: A one-time route that creates the admin account, protected by a secret stored in the server settings.
purpose: Creates the first admin login for the app.
why: Likely reason: lets the owner create the admin account once, without a public sign-up path for it.
how: Checks that the setup secret matches the SETUP_SECRET environment value, checks that no admin exists yet, checks the password is at least 8 characters, hashes it with bcrypt, then saves the admin user.
inputs: adminPassword and setupSecret in the request body.
outputs: A success message with the admin email, or an error: 403 for a wrong secret, 409 if the admin already exists, 400 for a short password, 500 for other failures.
risks: The admin email is written into the code, so changing the admin means editing the code. If the secret is weak or leaked, someone else could create the admin account first.
debug: 403 means the secret does not match SETUP_SECRET in the server settings. 409 means the admin already exists. Check userExists and createUser in lib/kv if the account is not saved.
